LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.2: Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: where do your parents work?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify family members by their names and professions
2. apply appropriate intonation and stress in pronouncing words for fluency
3. appreciate the role of immediate family members for social co- existence

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation

Teach
• Focus skill: identify family members by their names and professions.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. where do your parents work?
2. Why is it good to pronounce words correctly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
